Subject: Re: Air-gap deployment questions — artifact transfer and signing

Hi Hiro,

Thanks for taking this. We're preparing to pull the first offline bundle from Redwood for our air-gapped cluster (private deployment in our on-prem datacenter). Before we finalize the connector runbook, two quick asks:

1) We need a clear, minimal manifest for the bundle so our build team can validate checksums offline.
2) What does Redwood recommend for public key exchange and rotation for signed images? We prefer not to accept long-lived keys inside our network.

Also: are there any runtime configuration values embedded in images that we should scrub or overwite at deploy time? Our security team flagged a previous vendor that baked telemetry endpoints into the image.

Attachment: none in this message — we can send a sample manifest if helpful.

Greg

Subject: Re: Air-gap deployment questions — artifact transfer and signing

Greg — thanks for the clear questions. High-level answers below, and I attached a draft handoff checklist that mirrors what we run in Dedicated/Private air-gap projects.

1) Manifest: we provide a simple CSV manifest (filename, size bytes, sha256hex, sigfile). The manifest is detached (not embedded) so you can validate everything before extracting. Example fields are in the attached artifacts-manifest.csv template.

2) Key exchange & rotation: we support two models:
  - Customer-managed keys (recommended): you generate an ephemeral signing key pair in your HSM or KMS, provide the public key to Redwood during onboarding, and we sign artifacts per-release. We retain no customer private key.
  - Redwood-signed with short-lived key: Redwood will sign artifacts with a short-lived key and provide you the public key bundle plus a signed key certificate. You then verify signature and rotate the provided public key on your side per your rotation policy.

Rotation cadence we recommend: quarterly for air-gapped customers who manage keys externally; monthly for short-lived Redwood-signed workflows. We'll include a rotation plan template.

3) Embedded config: we do not bake telemetry endpoints into the runtime images. Runtime configuration is injected at bootstrap via configuration overlay (files in /etc/redwood/config.d) and environment variables. We will provide a scrub report for the bundle build.

Next steps: please send the target bundle transport method (USB + encrypted container OR SFTP-to-airgap-gateway) and your preferred key-management model. If you want, we can schedule a 30-min walkthrough with your infra and security teams.

I've attached: artifacts-manifest.csv (template) and handoff-checklist.md (workflows).

—hiro
Hiro Tanaka
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Greg — received, thanks. Quick answers and an actionable checklist below.

- We produce per-artifact signatures: each image (.tgz/.tar) will have a corresponding .sig file. Manifests are detached and signed independently.

- Rotation & re-signing: if you rotate verification keys, there are two supported approaches:
  1) Re-sign in-place: Redwood will re-sign the stored artifact archive with the new key and provide a re-signed .sig and new public cert bundle. That is the cleanest path but requires a new offline transfer if you do not allow remote fetch.
  2) Layered verification: include both the old and new public keys in your offline trust bundle for the overlap period. You keep both .sig files for audit; the runtime will accept either signature during the transition window.

Actionable checklist for pilot (we attached handoff-checklist.md and signing-key-rotation-plan.pdf):
- Confirm transport method: SFTP-to-airgap-gateway (recommended) OR sealed USB crate (requires chain-of-custody).
- Confirm key model: customer-managed (Acme vault) — Redwood will only sign with a per-release delegated key (we don't keep your private key).
- Verify manifest checksums and file sizes against artifacts-manifest.csv (we provide a verification script in the bundle).
- Install public key(s) into your offline trust store under /etc/redwood/trust.d/ and set rotation policy file /etc/redwood/trust.d/rotation.conf.
- Validate bootstrap by running verify.sh (included) and then a dry-run deploy with --no-restart to confirm overlays.

P.S. Laura — marissa flagged chain-of-custody form. I've attached a minimal custody PDF for your review.

We'll be on standby to schedule a walkthrough; propose Tue 05/04 10am PDT.

Thanks — hiro
